questions.q: What is AWS Security Hub's actual role, according to this lesson?
options: It aggregates and normalizes findings from services like GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and Config into one consistent format — it does not detect threats itself
It replaces GuardDuty entirely and performs all threat detection on its own
It is a firewall service that blocks malicious traffic before it reaches an EC2 instance
It only works with on-premises servers, not AWS resources
questions.explain: Security Hub's core value is normalization and aggregation into the AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF); the actual detection is done by contributing services like GuardDuty.

questions.q: What does GuardDuty require you to deploy in order to generate its core detections?
options: A dedicated hardware appliance in each AWS region
No agent or sensor — it analyzes existing sources like CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs
A third-party SIEM license purchased separately
A manually maintained list of every IP address to block
questions.explain: GuardDuty's core detections are agentless — it continuously analyzes log and event sources you're already generating, such as CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS query logs.

questions.q: A GuardDuty finding is named UnauthorizedAccess:EC2/SSHBruteForce. What does this naming convention tell you?
options: Nothing — finding names are random strings with no structure
Only the AWS region where the finding occurred
The threat purpose (unauthorized access), the affected resource type (EC2), and the threat family/mechanism (SSH brute-forcing) — readable without opening the console
That the finding was generated by AWS Config, not GuardDuty
questions.explain: GuardDuty's naming convention is ThreatPurpose:ResourceTypeAffected/ThreatFamilyName.DetectionMechanism, deliberately readable so you understand the nature of the detection at a glance.

questions.q: How do GuardDuty findings reach Security Hub?
options: They must be manually exported from GuardDuty and re-imported into Security Hub
They require a custom-built EventBridge integration written by the account owner
GuardDuty findings never appear in Security Hub under any configuration
GuardDuty findings flow into Security Hub automatically once both services are enabled in the same account and region
questions.explain: The integration between GuardDuty and Security Hub is automatic once both are enabled in the same account and region — no custom integration code is required for the findings to appear.

questions.q: What role do security standards like the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark play inside Security Hub?
options: Security Hub continuously checks resources against these standards and rolls the compliant/non-compliant results into a per-standard security score
They are legal documents with no automated checks in Security Hub
They only apply to GuardDuty findings, not to Security Hub
They replace the need for GuardDuty or Inspector entirely
questions.explain: Security Hub runs continuous checks against enabled standards (CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices, PCI DSS, etc.) and scores the account per standard based on passing and failing controls.
